reasoning: The claim that Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short and 5 feet 2 inches tall is a widespread historical misconception. Napoleon's height was recorded at his death as 5 feet 2 inches in pre-metric French units (*pieds* and *pouces*). Because a French inch (2.7 cm) was longer than an English inch (2.54 cm), 5 feet 2 inches in French measurements converts to approximately 5 feet 6.5 inches (1.68 meters) in standard modern Imperial units. Average male height in early 19th-century France was around 5 feet 5 inches, meaning Napoleon was actually average or slightly taller than average for his era.
